statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6469 (PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE ALTER TYPE resets extended statistics ownership) in 16.15 on the PostgreSQL 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6469/ lists 16.15 as the fixed release for major version 16 (versions before 16.15 are affected), and the 16.15 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.15/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/7c3367ab5dc42c34788cf9a4c768d46d4acf1041 on the REL_16_STABLE branch, which changes src/backend/commands/statscmds.c, tablecmds.c and src/backend/tcop/utility.c so that extended statistics objects rebuilt by ALTER TABLE ... ALTER TYPE keep their previous owner; it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-6469 and is in the REL_16_15 release tag and not in REL_16_14. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the files this fix changes. It lists CVE-2026-6469 under its 16.15-r0 secfixes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres, in every postgresql16 build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI package repository as of 2026-11-28, on both x86_64 and aarch64 (package checksums verified against the package index): 16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0 report PostgreSQL 16.13 and 16.14 and are affected, while 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 report PostgreSQL 16.15 and 16.16 and carry the fix. This fix adds no distinctive message string or exported symbol (the one error message it adds already exists in the earlier builds), so the per-build evidence is the version each server binary reports. 16.15-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6469, ALTER TABLE ALTER TYPE reassigning ownership of dependent extended statistics objects to the current user, which wrongly lets the table owner run DROP STATISTICS and ALTER STATISTICS on them and denies those commands to the prior owner, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6469/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6469. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
